summary: Agricola is a tense worker-placement farming game where taking an action denies it to everyone else that round, forcing constant recalculation as you build fields, pastures, and a house while keeping your family fed. The harvest phases are the crunch point where under-preparation gets brutally punished.
praised: huge variety from occupation and minor improvement cards
strong sense of building a coherent, self-sufficient farm
criticised: harsh food-penalty scoring feels punishing to newcomers
card-heavy deck can be swingy or push toward solitaire optimization

interaction.kind: worker placement action-space blocking plus a shared pool of occupation/minor-improvement cards
interaction.detail: Every round players claim single-use action spaces (wood, clay, the various improvement/occupation card draws, breeding spaces), so a good move often denies a resource or card an opponent was clearly building toward. Most of the actual farm-building — fencing, planting, feeding — happens on each player's own board, so the shared layer is the action-space race, not the scoring itself.
interaction.said: Reviewers often note Agricola rewards "denying the next player the action you just took" and that with 3-4 players the board "gets tight fast" as occupation/improvement cards and key action spaces get sniped; it's not usually called "solitaire" so much as "a tight race for spaces"

scoring.how_you_win: Build the best-rounded farm across fields, pastures, animals and house/family size while playing occupation and improvement cards for bonus points, avoiding empty spaces and unfed family members; highest total after 14 rounds wins.
